meta.title: Fuel index calculator — check your transport surcharge
meta.description: Free, no sign-up: enter your contract formula, your reference index and the invoiced rate, and get the gap in points and in euros.

fuel.h1: Is your fuel surcharge calculated correctly?
fuel.lede: Enter your contract formula, the indices for the period and the rate applied on your invoice. You get the gap straight away, in points and in euros.
fuel.privacy: The calculation runs entirely in your browser. No data is sent, stored or kept. No sign-up is required.

baseAmount.label: Base amount excluding VAT for the period
baseAmount.help: The transport amount before the fuel surcharge, for one shipment or for the whole month.

fuelShare.label: Fuel share set in the contract
fuelShare.help: The share of the price treated as fuel-sensitive. Most often between 20 and 35%.

baseIndex.label: Base index (contractual reference)
baseIndex.help: The index the contract sets as the starting point for indexation.

periodIndex.label: Index for the invoiced period
periodIndex.help: The index published for the month the invoice covers.

invoicedRate.label: Surcharge rate applied on the invoice
invoicedRate.help: The fuel surcharge percentage the carrier charged you.

errors.required: This field is needed for the calculation.
errors.positive: Enter a number greater than zero.

result.title: Result

verdict.aligned: The invoiced rate matches your formula. No significant gap for this period.
verdict.overcharged: The invoiced rate is above the expected rate. For this period the difference is {amount}.
verdict.undercharged: The invoiced rate is below the expected rate. For this period the difference is {amount} in your favour.

result.annualHint: Carried across twelve months of similar volumes, this gap would represent roughly {amount}.

formula.title: How the calculation works
formula.expression: Surcharge rate = fuel share × (period index − base index) ÷ base index
formula.explanation: This is the most widespread indexation formula in road transport contracts. It applies the relative movement of the index to the fraction of the price treated as fuel-sensitive.
formula.caveat: If your contract uses a different mechanism — a rolling average over several months, a trigger threshold, quarterly revision, indexation on pump prices rather than an index — the result above is only an approximation. Check the clause before raising it with your carrier.

source.title: Where to find your index
source.body: Your contract names the reference index to use. Take the one it states: changing the index changes the result.
source.placeholder: Index source and commercial reuse terms to be confirmed before publication.

fuel.disclaimer: This tool gives an indication of the calculation. It is neither legal advice nor a contractual analysis, and it does not certify that an invoice is correct. A gap found is a point to raise with your carrier.

cta.h2: Twelve months of invoices, every carrier, in one go
cta.text: This calculator handles one line at a time. In CarrierBridge you enter your formula once and the gap is tracked automatically, month after month, for each of your carriers — alongside your rate sheets and ancillary charges.
